title: Zero and Place Value
description: Learners build a number from 0 to 9,999 in a place value table and see it at the same time in Hindu-Arabic digits, in a South Asian digit set (Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil or Eastern Arabic style for Urdu) and in Roman numerals. Empty places glow, and a Hide the zeros option shows how the number changes when the zero symbol is removed.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
History of mathematics
Place value
Zero
Numeral systems
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Explain why a symbol for zero makes a place value system work.
Compare a place value system with Roman numerals, which have no zero and no place value.
Read the same number in Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil and Eastern Arabic style digits.
prerequisites: Counting and writing numbers up to 9,999
Knowing that a script is a writing system (Chapter 6)
keyQuestions: What job does a zero do inside a number like 507?
Why don't Roman numerals need a zero?
How do the digits 0 to 9 look in scripts used across South Asia?
misconceptions: Zero was invented by one person on one day.
A zero inside a number means nothing, so it can be left out.
Arabic numerals were invented by Arabs.
Every South Asian script has always had a zero digit.
